decisions.reason: A low-investment delivery program that is only mentioned on the website, it carries little public commitment, but it fits the firm's announced emphasis on speed and service, so it is likely kept or folded into the broader express offer.
The 72-hour program needs operational effort but little sunk investment and only modest visibility, so it could be consolidated, yet it is likely kept as part of the express-delivery positioning.

The firm invested in European certification and publicly launched the door at the BAU trade fair on its home page as part of the Teckentrup 62 modular system, so dropping it would write off a visible, sunk commitment.
The express program for doors and gates has its own dedicated page and is central to the announced fast-response service promise, so public commitment favors keeping it.

The online ordering and digital services platform involved substantial development investment, has its own page, and supports the strategic direction toward deeper service, so any early disappointment would be attributed to the start-up phase.
The certified fire and smoke protection door is part of the core certified product portfolio, where approval costs are sunk, so it is likely kept.
